newsitem.title: USA: Apple sees 20 pct plus FY97 gross margins.
newsitem.headline: Apple sees 20 pct plus FY97 gross margins.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson said the company expects gross margins to remain at or above 20 percent in fiscal 1997 as it strives to limit quarterly operating expenses to $500 million.

Anderson said in a conference call with analysts he would not forecast bottom-line results for the current first fiscal quarter, but that revenues should be roughly flat from the $2.32 billion it reported in the three months to September 27.
Apple's target for layoffs has been reduced to 1,500 from its previous goal of 2,800, he said, with 900 employees having been laid off under the program since January.
The Apple chief financial officer said the company is already some 90 percent of the way along in its plan to reduce its break even rate to the $2.0 billion revenue level.

In answer to questions from analysts, he said he expects inventories to be in the $650 million to $750 million range in the next few quarters, with no reason it should exceed the $750 million despite upcoming product introductions.
Apple's order backlog fell to $378 million at the end of its fourth fiscal quarter, compared with $428 million at the end of the sequentially earlier quarter, he said.

"I'm not going to make a forecast in terms of Q1 in terms of bottom line," Anderson said. But he noted management expects first quarter revenues to be relatively flat sequentially and operating expenses to be "fairly" comparable to slightly higher, due to consumer advertising.

"On gross margin, we feel good it can be at or above 20 percent," he added. He repeated the company expects to reach sustainable profitability by the end of the second quarter, but he would not make projections for bottom-line performance during the intervening months.
